<p>A hands-on Microsoft Excel workbook that demonstrates core-to-intermediate Excel skills across <strong>three realistic datasets</strong>: student grades, sales transactions, and employee records. Each sheet combines clean raw data, calculated columns, and a dedicated "function showcase" area, all with a consistent colour-coding system.</p>

<h2 id="-1-project-overview" style="--c:#00A86B">📘 1. Project Overview</h2>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Item</th>
<th>Details</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>Tool</strong></td>
<td>Microsoft Excel (uses modern functions such as <code>XLOOKUP</code> / <code>XMATCH</code>)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Sheets</strong></td>
<td>3: <code>Students Grade</code>, <code>Sales Data</code>, <code>Employee Data</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Records</strong></td>
<td>20 per sheet (60 total)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Currency</strong></td>
<td>Indian Rupee (₹)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>Goal</strong></td>
<td>Practise and demonstrate the practical use of logical, lookup, statistical, text, date and reference functions, plus professional formatting</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>Concepts covered:</strong> arithmetic and aggregate formulas, nested <code>IF</code>, <code>IF</code> with <code>AND</code>/<code>OR</code>, date arithmetic, rounding, lookups (<code>VLOOKUP</code>, <code>XLOOKUP</code>, <code>INDEX</code>+<code>MATCH</code>, <code>XMATCH</code>), conditional aggregation (<code>COUNTIF(S)</code>, <code>SUMIF(S)</code>, <code>AVERAGEIF(S)</code>), dynamic references (<code>INDIRECT</code>, <code>OFFSET</code>) and text formatting (<code>TEXT</code>).</p>

<h2 id="-3-colour-coding--formatting-system" style="--c:#2980B9">🎨 3. Colour Coding &amp; Formatting System</h2>

<ul>

<h3 id="-42-formulas-explained" style="--c:#16A085">🟣 4.2 Formulas explained</h3>
<p><strong>Total Marks (G)</strong></p>
<pre><code class="language-excel">=SUM(C2:E2)
</code></pre>
<p>Example: Student 1 → 61 + 48 + 76 = <strong>185</strong>.</p>
<p><strong>Average (H)</strong></p>
<pre><code class="language-excel">=ROUND(AVERAGE(C2:E2),2)
</code></pre>
<p>Example: 185 / 3 = <strong>61.67</strong>.</p>
<p><strong>Grade (I)</strong>: nested <code>IF</code> on the average</p>
<pre><code class="language-excel">=IF(H2&gt;=80,&quot;A&quot;,IF(H2&gt;=60,&quot;B&quot;,&quot;C&quot;))
</code></pre>
<p>Observed behaviour: averages of 84.33, 95 → <strong>A</strong>; 61.67–78.33 → <strong>B</strong>; 55–59 → <strong>C</strong>. The cut-offs (80 / 60) are consistent with every row.</p>
<p><strong>Result (J)</strong>: every student shows <strong>Pass</strong> (all subject marks are 40 or higher, so a pass-mark rule is met).</p>
<pre><code class="language-excel">=IF(H2&gt;=40,&quot;Pass&quot;,&quot;Fail&quot;)
</code></pre>
<p><strong>Age (K)</strong>: whole years since enrollment</p>
<pre><code class="language-excel">=DATEDIF(F2,TODAY(),&quot;Y&quot;)
</code></pre>
<p>Example: 1/1/2018 → <strong>8</strong> years (as of Oct 2026). Students enrolled within the last year show <strong>0</strong>.</p>
<p><strong>IF with AND (L)</strong>: multi-condition eligibility test</p>
<pre><code class="language-excel">=IF(AND(C2&gt;=80, &lt;second condition&gt;),&quot;Eligible&quot;,&quot;Not Eligible&quot;)
</code></pre>
<p>Observed behaviour: every student with <strong>Math ≥ 80</strong> is <em>Eligible</em> (80, 82, 83, 85, 90, 93, 94, 97, 98) and every student below 80 is <em>Not Eligible</em> (even 78). This demonstrates how <code>AND()</code> requires <strong>all</strong> conditions to be true.</p>
<p><strong>Students with Math &gt; 60 (M2)</strong></p>
<pre><code class="language-excel">=COUNTIF(C2:C21,&quot;&gt;60&quot;)
</code></pre>
<p>Result <strong>19</strong> (only Student 9 scored 41).</p>

<h3 id="-52-formulas-explained" style="--c:#2980B9">🟢 5.2 Formulas explained</h3>
<p><strong>Discount slab (G)</strong>: nested <code>IF</code></p>
<pre><code class="language-excel">=IF(E2&gt;=25000,&quot;10%Discount&quot;,IF(E2&gt;=10000,&quot;5%Discount&quot;,&quot;No Discount&quot;))
</code></pre>
<p>Observed behaviour: amounts under about ₹10,000 → <em>No Discount</em>; about ₹15,000–₹24,000 → <em>5%</em>; ₹30,000 and above → <em>10%</em>. (The exact upper cut-off lies between ₹23,672 and ₹30,436.)</p>
<p><strong>Discount Eligible (H)</strong>: combines two conditions with <code>OR</code></p>
<pre><code class="language-excel">=IF(OR(C2=&quot;South&quot;,E2&gt;=25000),&quot;Eligible&quot;,&quot;Not eligible&quot;)
</code></pre>
<p>Observed behaviour: <strong>all South-region sales are Eligible</strong> (even small ones like ₹7,048), while sales from other regions are Eligible only for large amounts.</p>
<p><strong>Ceiling Amount (I)</strong></p>
<pre><code class="language-excel">=CEILING(E2,100)      // 7,048 → 7,100
</code></pre>
<p><strong>Floor Amount (J)</strong></p>
<pre><code class="language-excel">=FLOOR(E2,100)        // 7,048 → 7,000
</code></pre>

<td><code>Finance</code></td>
<td><code>=XLOOKUP(3001,A2:A21,C2:C21)</code></td>
<td>Returns the department of Employee 1</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>INDEX + MATCH SALARY</strong></td>
<td><code>86766</code></td>
<td><code>=INDEX(D2:D21,MATCH(3001,A2:A21,0))</code></td>
<td>Classic two-function lookup, returning salary</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>INDEX + MATCH DEPARTMENT</strong></td>
<td><code>Finance</code></td>
<td><code>=INDEX(C2:C21,MATCH(3001,A2:A21,0))</code></td>
<td>Same technique, returning department</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>HR DEPT_TOTAL SALARY</strong></td>
<td><code>417713</code></td>
<td><code>=SUMIFS(D2:D21,C2:C21,"HR")</code></td>
<td>Conditional sum using <code>SUMIFS</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>DEPARTMENT TOTAL SALARY</strong></td>
<td><code>485714</code></td>
<td><code>=SUMIF(C2:C21,"Finance",D2:D21)</code></td>
<td>Total Finance salary</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><strong>DATEIF Function</strong></td>
<td><code>11</code></td>
<td><code>=DATEDIF(E2,TODAY(),"Y")</code></td>
<td>Years of service (Jan 2015 → Oct 2026 = 11)</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<h2 id="-8-issues-found--recommended-fixes" style="--c:#2C3E50">🛠️ 8. Issues Found &amp; Recommended Fixes</h2>
<p>Reviewing the output screenshots turned up the following items worth correcting before presenting or publishing the workbook.</p>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>#</th>
<th>Sheet / Cell</th>
<th>Issue</th>
<th>Recommended fix</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>1</td>
<td>Students Grade <code>K20:K21</code></td>
<td><strong><code>#NUM!</code> error.</strong> <code>DATEDIF</code> fails when the enrollment date is in the future (11/15/2026, 5/14/2027).</td>
<td><code>=IF(F20&gt;TODAY(),"Not enrolled yet",DATEDIF(F20,TODAY(),"Y"))</code>, or wrap in <code>IFERROR</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2</td>
<td>Students Grade <code>L</code></td>
<td>Typo <strong>"Egiible"</strong> appears in several rows (the formula text is spelled wrong).</td>
<td>Correct the string to <code>"Eligible"</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3</td>
<td>Sales Data <code>L3</code></td>
<td>Shows <code>6/23/1905</code>: the value <code>2001</code> is formatted as a <strong>date</strong>.</td>
<td>Set cell format to <strong>General</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4</td>
<td>Employee Data <code>K2</code></td>
<td>Shows <code>10/15/1911</code>, and <code>I3</code> shows <code>42005</code>: numbers formatted as dates, and a date formatted as a number.</td>
<td>Apply the correct Date / General format</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5</td>
<td>Employee Data <code>E19:E21</code></td>
<td>Joining dates are in the <strong>future</strong> (2026–2028), which is unrealistic for current employees.</td>
<td>Correct the dataset</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6</td>
<td>Sales Data headers</td>
<td>Spelling: <em>"Celling Amount"</em>, <em>"INDIRACT Function"</em>, <em>"Not eligible/Eligible"</em> casing inconsistent.</td>
<td>Rename to <em>Ceiling Amount</em>, <em>INDIRECT Function</em>; use one casing</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>7</td>
<td>Employee Data headers</td>
<td>Spelling: <em>"SUMIFC Fuction"</em>, <em>"COUNTIFC Fuction"</em>, <em>"AVARAGEIFC"</em>, <em>"DATEIFC"</em>, <em>"XLOOKUP Fuc"</em>, <em>"DEPARMENT"</em>.</td>
<td>Use <em>SUMIF Function</em>, <em>COUNTIF Function</em>, <em>AVERAGEIF Function</em>, <em>DATEDIF Function</em>, <em>XLOOKUP Function</em>, <em>DEPARTMENT</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>8</td>
<td>Employee Data <code>K4</code></td>
<td><code>D2+H2</code> references an empty cell (H2).</td>
<td>Change to <code>D2+F2</code> (or <code>=G2</code>)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>9</td>
<td>All sheets</td>
<td>Hard-coded thresholds (80, 60, 25000, 10%) inside formulas.</td>
<td>Move them to a small <strong>assumptions table</strong> and reference with absolute refs (<code>$</code>)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>10</td>
<td>All sheets</td>
<td>Plain ranges.</td>
<td>Convert data to <strong>Excel Tables</strong> (<code>Ctrl+T</code>) for structured references and auto-expanding formulas</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<h2 id="-9-skills-demonstrated" style="--c:#E91E63">🏆 9. Skills Demonstrated</h2>
<ul>
<li>Structuring data into clean, analysis-ready tables</li>
<li>Building calculated columns with arithmetic, logical and date functions</li>
<li>Writing nested and multi-condition logic (<code>IF</code>, <code>AND</code>, <code>OR</code>)</li>
<li>Performing exact-match lookups with both legacy and modern functions</li>
<li>Summarising data conditionally by category (<code>SUMIF</code>, <code>COUNTIF</code>, <code>AVERAGEIF</code>)</li>
<li>Working with dynamic references (<code>INDIRECT</code>, <code>OFFSET</code>)</li>
<li>Professional presentation: consistent colour coding, borders, number formats and currency formatting</li>
<li>Spotting and diagnosing formula errors (<code>#NUM!</code>, wrong cell formats)</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="-10-how-to-use-this-workbook" style="--c:#27AE60">🚀 10. How to Use This Workbook</h2>
<ol>
<li>Open the <code>.xlsx</code> file in <strong>Excel 2021 / Microsoft 365</strong> (required for <code>XLOOKUP</code> and <code>XMATCH</code>).</li>
<li>Switch between the three tabs at the bottom: <strong>Students Grade</strong>, <strong>Sales Data</strong>, <strong>Employee Data</strong>.</li>
<li>Edit any <strong>cream</strong> (input) cell and watch the <strong>purple</strong> (calculated) cells update automatically.</li>
<li>Change the lookup keys (e.g. an Employee ID or Sales ID) inside the <strong>green</strong> showcase formulas to test each function.</li>
<li>Press <code>Ctrl + ~</code> to toggle formula view and inspect every formula.</li>
</ol>
